items.title: Show HN: A fullscreen Game of Life in which every board is a runnable program
items.contentSnippet:
Each tile is a Piet program that prints a word.
Each generation, every tile runs.
After, its label shows what it printed.
The original was a Piet program, compiled from Temper by a backend I wrote, playing Life on another Piet program:
3 hours, 1.27 billion steps. Generation 0 printed "Piet!".

items.title: Show HN: Sibuna an open source web application firewall with proof of work
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN,
We are building an open source web application firewall Sibuna to have more control over automated traffic from AI bots and crawlers.
Sibuna runs as a reverse proxy or alongside an existing ingress through forward-auth. It includes application inspection, OWASP CRS support and a wasm based management console.
Please try it, and give us feedback for improvements.
Github Project: https://github.com/insanai/sibuna

items.title: Show HN: World Watcher – a map to seamlessly watch public webcam streams
items.contentSnippet:
World Watcher is an interactive map of live webcams around the world, that prioritizes smooth UX and correct geolocation of cameras.
The idea is to have a better experience of navigating live webcam streams that are publicly available on YouTube. There were already a few livecam aggregators out there that include a map, but I found none of them satisfying to use, as they always require you to open new pages to watch the streams. On World Watcher, you can jump from place to place seamlessly.

items.title: Show HN: AntiPDF – PDF as it should have been all along
items.contentSnippet:
Hi HN,
I built AntiPDF, a native PDF reader AND editor for Windows (coming to Linux and MacOS).
I built it because I got tired of getting ads and all those Acrobatics.
AntiPDF can read, edit, annotate, OCR and organize PDFs while keeping your documents on your computer. It's written completely in Odin and rendered with Vulkan using MSDF fonts for those lovely smooth fonts.
